Sanjay vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 August, 2015
 Crr-1832-2015
 (Sanjay Vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh)
13-08-2015
Shri Manish Tiwari, learned counsel for the applicant.

sentences.text:
Shri Amit Kumar Pandey, learned Panel Lawyer for
respondent/State.
Heard arguments on the question of admission of this revision.
Having perused the impugned judgment and the memo of revision, this revision being arguable is admitted for final hearing.
Learned Panel Lawyer has taken notice of admission of this revision on behalf of the respondent/State.
Hence, no further notice is required to be sent to it.

Heard on I.A. No. 15248/2015, which is the first application under Section 397(1) of the Cr.P.C.
moved on behalf of the applicant for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to him during the pendency of this revision.

Vide impugned judgment dated 31.07.2015 passed by the VIth Additional Session Judge, Sagar in CRA No. 433/2014 Sanjay Vs. State of M.P., the applicant stands convicted under Section 7(1)/16(A)(1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and sentenced thereunder to suffer rigorous imprisonment for a term of one year with a fine of Rs. 1000/-, with default stipulation.

entities.text: CRA No. 433/2014 Sanjay Vs. State of M.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant remained on bail during the trial of the case and the pendency of appeal.

However, he has been suffering the jail sentence since 31.07.2015,
the date of impugned judgment.
It is also submitted by him that the revision is of the year 2015 and there is no likelihood of this revision being listed for final hearing in recent future.

It is also submitted by him that looking to the quantum of remaining jail sentence, this revision becomes infructuous in case the applicant would have suffered it before this revision being decided on merits.
It is also submitted by him that he has a good case on merits.
Upon these submissions, learned counsel prays to allow the I.A. Learned Panel Lawyer opposes the prayer.

Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case, the submissions raised on behalf of the parties by their counsel and the short term of jail sentence, but without commenting on the merits of the case, I am of the view that this is fit case for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail to the applicant, therefore, the IA is allowed.
The execution of remaining jail sentence of the applicant is hereby suspended and it is ordered that he shall be released on bail upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) with one solvent surety of the same amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, subject to depositing of fine amount, if any.
On being released on bail, the applicant shall appear before the Registry of this Court first time on Sanjay vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 August, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147059527/
1 04.10.2015 and thereafter on all such dates as may be fixed by it in this regard until further orders.
Record of the courts below be called for.
List the case for final hearing after receipt of records in due course.
Certified copy as per rules.
(RAJENDRA MAHAJAN) JUDGE Sanjay vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 August, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147059527/
